question_html: Under Section 2(30) of the Companies Act, 2013, how are debentures defined?

options.A: Instruments that grant ownership rights in a company.
options.B: Includes debenture stock, bonds or any other instrument of a company evidencing a debt, whether constituting a charge on assets or not[cite: 13].
options.C: Only instruments that carry a mandatory first floating charge on all assets.
options.D: Short-term commercial paper issued exclusively to scheduled banks.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Section 2(30) defines debentures as including debenture stock, bonds or any other instrument evidencing a debt, whether constituting a charge on assets or not[cite: 13].

question_html: Can a company issue debentures carrying voting rights under the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: Yes, if approved by a special resolution.
options.B: No company shall issue any debentures carrying any voting rights[cite: 13].
options.C: Yes, only in the event of default in interest payment for two consecutive years.
options.D: Yes, if they are fully convertible debentures.

answer_html: Answer: (B) The statute explicitly states that no company shall issue any debentures carrying any voting rights[cite: 13].

question_html: What is the status of debenture holders in relation to the company?

options.A: Owners of the company
options.B: Creditors of the company[cite: 13]
options.C: Management partners
options.D: Guarantors of the share capital

answer_html: Answer: (B) Debenture holders are the creditors of the company, whereas shareholders are the owners[cite: 13].

question_html: How is interest on debentures treated for tax determination purposes compared to dividends?

options.A: Both are appropriations of profit and non-deductible.
options.B: Debenture interest is a charge against profits and deductible as an expense, whereas dividends are appropriations of profit and not deductible[cite: 13].
options.C: Dividends are tax-deductible expenses, while debenture interest is an appropriation.
options.D: Neither is deductible in determining taxable profit.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Debenture interest is a charge against profits and deductible as an expense, while dividends are appropriations of profit and non-deductible[cite: 13].

question_html: Can debentures be forfeited by a company for non-payment of call moneys, similar to shares?

options.A: Yes, under the same provisions as equity shares.
options.B: No, debentures cannot be forfeited for non-payment of call moneys[cite: 13].
options.C: Yes, but only if approved by debenture trustees.
options.D: Yes, after serving a mandatory 30-day notice.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Unlike shares, debentures cannot be forfeited for non-payment of call moneys[cite: 13].

question_html: Where are debentures presented in a company's Balance Sheet as per Schedule III?

options.A: Shareholder's Funds
options.B: Long-Term Borrowings[cite: 13]
options.C: Trade Payables
options.D: Short-Term Provisions

answer_html: Answer: (B) In the company's Balance Sheet, debentures are shown under 'Long Term Borrowings'[cite: 13].

question_html: What is a 'fixed charge' on assets in the context of secured debentures?

options.A: A general charge covering all present and future assets of the company.
options.B: A mortgage on specific assets which cannot be sold without the consent of debenture holders[cite: 13].
options.C: A floating encumbrance over current assets like inventory and debtors.
options.D: An unsecured promise to pay interest on specific dates.

answer_html: Answer: (B) A fixed charge is a mortgage on specific assets which cannot be sold without consent, and sale proceeds are utilized first to repay debenture holders[cite: 13].

question_html: What distinguishes 'Bearer Debentures' from 'Registered Debentures'?

options.A: Bearer debentures require a formal transfer deed registered with the company.
options.B: Bearer debentures are transferable by mere delivery and no record of holders is kept by the company[cite: 13].
options.C: Registered debentures are negotiable instruments payable to whoever holds the physical certificate.
options.D: Bearer debentures require recording name and address in the Register of Debenture holders.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Bearer debentures are transferable by delivery and no record of holders is maintained by the company[cite: 13].

question_html: What are 'Irredeemable Debentures' also known as?

options.A: Convertible bonds
options.B: Perpetual debentures[cite: 13]
options.C: Naked debentures
options.D: Collateral debentures

answer_html: Answer: (B) Irredeemable debentures are not repayable during the lifetime of the company and are also called perpetual debentures[cite: 13].

question_html: In terms of priority on winding up, how do First Mortgage Debentures rank?

options.A: Payable after equity shareholders.
options.B: Payable after satisfying second mortgage debentures.
options.C: Payable first out of the property charged[cite: 13].
options.D: Payable pari passu with unsecured trade creditors.

answer_html: Answer: (C) First mortgage debentures are payable first out of the property charged[cite: 13].

question_html: When debentures are issued at par and redeemable at a premium, what account is debited at the time of allotment for the premium payable on redemption?

options.A: Securities Premium Account
options.B: Loss on Issue of Debentures Account[cite: 13]
options.C: Debenture Redemption Reserve Account
options.D: Discount on Issue of Debentures Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Premium payable on redemption represents a loss to the company and is debited to Loss on Issue of Debentures Account at the time of allotment[cite: 13].
topic_text: Issue of Debentures - Redeemable at Premium

question_html: What is the nature of the 'Debenture Redemption Premium Account'?

options.A: Real Account representing intangible assets
options.B: Nominal Account representing capital loss
options.C: Personal Account representing a liability of the company[cite: 13]
options.D: Revenue reserve representing accumulated profits

answer_html: Answer: (C) Debenture Redemption Premium Account is a personal account which represents a liability of the company in respect of premium payable on redemption[cite: 13].

question_html: Why must premium payable on the redemption of debentures be recognized at the time of issue itself?

options.A: In compliance with SEBI guidelines for public listings.
options.B: Considering the principle of conservatism or prudence to account for anticipated future losses[cite: 13].
options.C: Because the Companies Act mandates cash escrow before issue.
options.D: To offset current year tax liabilities.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Recognition of redemption premium at issue follows the principle of conservatism or prudence, acknowledging the future obligation and loss[cite: 13].

question_html: Agrotech Ltd. issued 150 lakh 9% debentures of ₹100 each at a discount of 6%, redeemable at a premium of 5% after 3 years. What is the total amount of Loss on Issue of Debentures to be recorded?

options.A: ₹900 lakhs
options.B: ₹750 lakhs
options.C: ₹1,650 lakhs[cite: 13]
options.D: ₹150 lakhs

answer_html: Answer: (C) Total loss = Discount on issue (6% of ₹100 = ₹6) + Premium on redemption (5% of ₹100 = ₹5) $\times$ 150 lakh debentures = ₹11 $\times$ 150 lakh = ₹1,650 lakhs[cite: 13].
topic_text: Calculation of Loss on Issue of Debentures

question_html: Does the Companies Act impose any restriction on the percentage of discount at which debentures can be issued, similar to shares?

options.A: Yes, discount cannot exceed 10% of face value.
options.B: Yes, discount cannot exceed 25% under any circumstances.
options.C: No, the Companies Act does not impose any restriction on the price or discount at which debentures can be issued[cite: 13].
options.D: Discount on debentures is completely prohibited by Section 53.

answer_html: Answer: (C) Unlike shares, the Companies Act does not impose any restriction on the price or discount at which debentures can be issued[cite: 13].

question_html: What is the effect of issuing debentures at a discount on the true rate of interest (effective borrowing cost)?

options.A: It decreases the true rate of interest below the coupon rate.
options.B: It has no impact on the true rate of interest.
options.C: It increases the true rate of interest payable above the coupon rate[cite: 13].
options.D: It makes the interest rate variable based on market indices.

answer_html: Answer: (C) Issuing debentures at a discount means receiving less cash while paying interest on the full nominal value, thereby increasing the true rate of interest[cite: 13].
topic_text: Effective Rate of Interest on Discounted Debentures

question_html: Which act governs the restrictions on the utilization of Securities Premium when debentures are issued at a premium?

options.A: Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act and Section 52 of the Companies Act, 2013[cite: 13]
options.B: Income Tax Act, 1961
options.C: Banking Regulation Act, 1949
options.D: MRTP Act

answer_html: Answer: (A) Debentures are covered under 'securities', so utilization of premium is governed by Section 52 of the Companies Act, 2013[cite: 13].

question_html: What is 'collateral security'?

options.A: The primary mortgage security created against a long-term loan.
options.B: Secondary or supporting security for a loan which can be realized if the original loan is not repaid on due date[cite: 13].
options.C: Unsecured debentures issued without any charge on assets.
options.D: Equity shares deposited as margin with commercial banks.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Collateral security means secondary or supporting security for a loan, realizable if the original loan is defaulted[cite: 13].

question_html: When debentures are issued as collateral security under Method 2, what account is debited?

options.A: Bank Loan Account
options.B: Debentures Suspense Account[cite: 13]
options.C: Loss on Issue of Debentures Account
options.D: Goodwill Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Under Method 2, Debentures Suspense Account is debited and % Debentures Account is credited[cite: 13].

question_html: Where does the 'Debentures Suspense Account' appear in the Balance Sheet under Method 2 of collateral security?

options.A: Equity and Liabilities side under Reserves and Surplus
options.B: Assets side under Non-Current / Current Assets (deducted or shown as other non-current asset)[cite: 13]
options.C: Contingent liabilities note only
options.D: Deducted directly from Long-Term Borrowings

answer_html: Answer: (B) Debentures Suspense Account appears on the assets side of the Balance Sheet under Other Non-Current Assets (or shown as a contra deduction from debentures)[cite: 13].

question_html: Are holders of debentures issued as collateral security entitled to interest on those debentures while the loan is running normally?

options.A: Yes, they receive interest on both the loan and the collateral debentures.
options.B: No, the holder of such debentures is entitled to interest only on the amount of loan, but not on the debentures[cite: 13].
options.C: Yes, at half the coupon rate.
options.D: Only if the loan defaults.

answer_html: Answer: (B) The holder of collateral debentures is entitled to interest only on the amount of loan, but not on the collateral debentures[cite: 13].

question_html: F Ltd. purchased machinery for a book value of ₹4,00,000 and paid consideration by issuing 10% debentures of ₹100 each at a premium of 25%. What amount was credited to the Debenture Account?
answer_html: Answer: (C) Number of debentures = ₹4,00,000 / ₹125 = 3,200 debentures. Debenture Account is credited with face value: 3,200 $\times$ ₹100 = ₹3,20,000[cite: 13].
topic_text: Issue of Debentures for Consideration Other than Cash

question_html: How should discount on the issue of debentures be amortized when debentures are redeemable after a certain fixed period in equal installments?

options.A: Written off entirely in the first year of issue.
options.B: Written off equally throughout the life of the debentures applying the straight-line method[cite: 13].
options.C: Written off in the ratio of declining balance of debentures.
options.D: Amortized only at the time of final redemption.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Total discount is written off equally throughout the life of the debentures using the straight-line method[cite: 13].

question_html: When debentures are redeemable at different dates (unequal installments), how should the total amount of discount on issue be written off?

options.A: Straight-line over 5 years regardless of redemption dates.
options.B: In the ratio of debenture amount outstanding in each year[cite: 13].
options.C: Accelerated write-off in the final year.
options.D: Equally divided by the number of redemption events.

answer_html: Answer: (B) When debentures are redeemed at different dates, discount is written off in the ratio of debenture amount outstanding in each year[cite: 13].
topic_text: Amortization of Discount for Unequal Redemptions

question_html: According to the Guidance Note and Accounting Standards (AS 16 / AS 26 scope), over what typical period of benefit is it acceptable to amortize ancillary borrowing costs and debenture discount?

options.A: Exactly 1 year
options.B: Typically 3 to 5 years (not exceeding loan tenure)[cite: 13]
options.C: 20 years
options.D: Indefinitely until company winds up

answer_html: Answer: (B) The Guidance Note clarified that amortizing these expenses over the period of benefit, typically 3 to 5 years, is acceptable[cite: 13].
topic_text: Period of Amortization of Borrowing Costs

question_html: How is interest on debentures calculated?

options.A: At coupon rate on the market price of debentures
options.B: At coupon rate on the nominal value of debentures[cite: 13]
options.C: At variable rates based on net profits of the company
options.D: At fixed rates on the issue price after deducting discount

answer_html: Answer: (B) Interest on debenture is paid periodically and calculated at the coupon rate on the nominal value of debentures[cite: 13].

question_html: Why does a company pay debenture interest net of Tax Deducted at Source (TDS)?

options.A: Because TDS is an internal company reserve.
options.B: Because the company is under statutory obligation to deduct tax at source as per Income Tax Act, 1961[cite: 13].
options.C: To reduce the coupon rate payable to investors.
options.D: To pay dividends to equity shareholders instead.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Companies must deduct tax at source under the Income Tax Act, 1961, and deposit it with tax authorities[cite: 13].

question_html: What is the nature of 'Premium on Redemption of Debentures Account' when it appears in the Balance Sheet?

options.A: Nominal account - income
options.B: Nominal account - expenditure
options.C: Personal account[cite: 13]
options.D: Real account

answer_html: Answer: (C) Premium on redemption of debentures account appearing in the balance sheet is a personal account representing a liability[cite: 13].

question_html: When are debentures issued at a discount in market practice?

options.A: When market interest rate is higher than debenture interest rate[cite: 13]
options.B: When market interest rate is lower than debenture interest rate
options.C: When market interest rate equals debenture interest rate
options.D: When company profits exceed expectations

answer_html: Answer: (A) The company issues debentures at a discount when the market rate of interest is higher than the debenture interest rate[cite: 13].
topic_text: Market Interest Rate and Issue Price

question_html: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Bearer Debentures?

options.A: They are treated as negotiable instruments.
options.B: Their transfer requires a deed of transfer[cite: 13].
options.C: They are transferable by mere delivery.
options.D: Interest is paid to the holder irrespective of identity.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Bearer debentures do not require any transfer deed; they are transferable by mere delivery[cite: 13].

question_html: What is the final entry for recording collateral debentures in the books under Method 2?

options.A: Credit Debentures A/c and debit Cash A/c.
options.B: Debit Debenture suspense A/c and credit Cash A/c.
options.C: Debit Debenture suspense A/c and credit Debentures A/c[cite: 13].
options.D: Debit Bank Loan A/c and credit Debenture suspense A/c.

answer_html: Answer: (C) Under Method 2, the entry is: Debenture Suspense A/c Dr. To % Debentures A/c[cite: 13].

question_html: When are debentures issued at a premium in market practice?

options.A: When market interest rate is higher than debenture interest rate
options.B: When market interest rate is lower than debenture interest rate[cite: 13]
options.C: When the issuing company suffers continuous losses
options.D: When debentures are unsecured and naked

answer_html: Answer: (B) A company issues debentures at a premium when the market rate of interest is lower than the debenture interest rate[cite: 13].

question_html: What is a floating charge on assets?

options.A: A mortgage on specific fixed land and buildings.
options.B: A charge that generally covers all the assets of the company including future ones[cite: 13].
options.C: A charge restricted to cash at bank only.
options.D: An illegal encumbrance that cannot be registered with RoC.

answer_html: Answer: (B) A floating charge generally covers all the assets of the company including future ones[cite: 13].

question_html: What happens to collateral debentures when the original bank loan is fully repaid on the due date?

options.A: They are permanently converted into equity shares.
options.B: They are at once released along with the main security[cite: 13].
options.C: They are sold by the lender in the open market.
options.D: They become first mortgage debentures automatically.

answer_html: Answer: (B) When the loan is repaid on the due date, these debentures are at once released with the main security[cite: 13].

question_html: What is the primary purpose of creating a trusteeship in favor of one or more persons in the case of mortgage debentures?

options.A: To manage the daily sales and revenue of the company.
options.B: To safeguard the interest of debenture holders with powers of a mortgagee[cite: 13].
options.C: To distribute dividends to equity shareholders.
options.D: To audit the annual financial statements.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Trustees of debenture holders have powers of a mortgagee and act to safeguard the interest of debenture holders[cite: 13].

question_html: If a company incurs a net loss during a financial year, is it legally excused from paying interest to its debenture holders?

options.A: Yes, interest is paid only out of profits like dividends.
options.B: No, even if the company incurs loss or earns profit, it has to pay interest on debentures because it is a charge against profits[cite: 13].
options.C: Yes, interest payment is automatically deferred until the next profitable year.
options.D: Only if debenture holders pass a special resolution waving interest.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Debenture interest is a charge against profits, payable whether there is profit or loss[cite: 13].

question_html: What are convertible debentures?

options.A: Debentures that can be converted into equity shares after a certain period of time[cite: 13].
options.B: Debentures that are convertible into bank loans at maturity.
options.C: Debentures that change their coupon rate annually.
options.D: Debentures that can be exchanged for bearer bonds.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Convertible debentures are those which will be converted into equity shares after a certain period of time[cite: 13].

question_html: What is the sequence of payment at the time of company liquidation regarding debenture holders and shareholders?

options.A: Equity shareholders are paid first, followed by debenture holders.
options.B: Debenture holders are paid off before shareholders on priority basis[cite: 13].
options.C: Preference shareholders, debenture holders, and equity shareholders rank equally.
options.D: Debenture holders rank after trade payables and shareholders.

answer_html: Answer: (B) At the time of liquidation, debenture holders are paid off before shareholders on a priority basis[cite: 13].

question_html: What are unsecured or 'naked' debentures?

options.A: Debentures secured by a floating charge on inventory.
options.B: Debentures that are not secured by any charge upon any assets[cite: 13].
options.C: Debentures issued without issuing a prospectus.
options.D: Debentures that do not carry any interest.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Unsecured or naked debentures are not secured by any charge upon any assets[cite: 13].

question_html: How are registered debentures transferred?

options.A: By mere physical delivery from hand to hand.
options.B: By complying with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and executing transfer deeds recorded in the register[cite: 13].
options.C: By endorsement on the back without company registration.
options.D: By passing an ordinary resolution in a general meeting.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Registered debentures require compliance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 for effecting transfer, as holder particulars are recorded in the register[cite: 13].

question_html: When debentures are issued at par and redeemable at par, what are the basic journal entries recorded upon receipt and allotment?

options.A: Bank A/c Dr. To Debenture Application A/c, followed by Debenture Application A/c Dr. To % Debentures A/c[cite: 13].
options.B: Debenture Application A/c Dr. To Securities Premium A/c.
options.C: Loss on Issue Dr. To Debentures A/c.
options.D: Discount on Issue Dr. To Bank A/c.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Bank A/c Dr. To Debenture Application A/c, and upon allotment, Debenture Application A/c Dr. To % Debentures A/c[cite: 13].
topic_text: Journal Entries for Par Issue and Par Redemption

question_html: What does a charge on assets imply in debenture documentation?

options.A: An encumbrance to meet obligations under the Trust Deed, giving lenders the right to secure payment from such assets[cite: 13].
options.B: A fee paid to the Registrar of Companies for incorporation.
options.C: A tax levied by the government on debt instruments.
options.D: A penalty charged for delayed interest payment.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Charge is an encumbrance under the Trust Deed where the company agrees to mortgage specific assets to secure payment[cite: 13].

question_html: What is the primary benefit of debt financing through debentures for a company?

options.A: It grants voting rights to bondholders to stabilize management.
options.B: It helps in reducing the cost of capital and designing an appropriate capital structure[cite: 13].
options.C: It permanently eliminates the need for any cash outflow.
options.D: It avoids registration with the Registrar of Companies.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Debt financing reduces the cost of capital and helps in designing an appropriate capital structure[cite: 13].

question_html: When debentures are issued at a discount and redeemable at a premium, how can the discount on issue and loss on redemption be treated in journal entries?

options.A: They must be kept in separate ledger accounts and never combined.
options.B: Discount on issue can be combined with Loss on issue of debentures as both represent loss/expense to the company[cite: 13].
options.C: Discount on issue is credited to Securities Premium.
options.D: Loss on redemption is ignored until the final year.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Discount on issue can be combined with loss on issue of debentures since both represent losses to the company[cite: 13].
topic_text: Combining Discount and Loss on Issue

question_html: In the accounting entries for debenture interest payment, what account is credited along with Bank when TDS is deducted?

options.A: Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) Payable Account[cite: 13]
options.B: Advance Tax Account
options.C: General Reserve Account
options.D: Debenture Holders Account

answer_html: Answer: (A) Debenture holders A/c Dr. To TDS Payable A/c, To Bank A/c[cite: 13].

question_html: What is the fixed value printed on a debenture certificate called?

options.A: Market value
options.B: Nominal or face value[cite: 13]
options.C: Issue price
options.D: Book value

answer_html: Answer: (B) Nominal or face value is the fixed value printed on the bond or certificate[cite: 13].

question_html: Where are both Discount on Issue of Debentures and Loss on Issue of Debentures shown in the Balance Sheet if they are to be written off over future accounting periods?

options.A: Non-current/current assets depending upon the period for which it has to be written off[cite: 13]
options.B: Under Shareholder's Funds as negative reserves
options.C: Under Current Liabilities as provisions
options.D: Deducted directly from Long-Term Borrowings

answer_html: Answer: (A) In the balance sheet both items (Discount and Loss) are shown as Non-current/current assets depending upon the period for amortization[cite: 13].
topic_text: Balance Sheet Presentation of Discount and Loss on Issue

question_html: How is the interest payable on coupon debentures classified in financial statements?

options.A: An appropriation of net profit
options.B: A charge against the profits of the company[cite: 13]
options.C: A direct reduction of share capital
options.D: A capital receipt

answer_html: Answer: (B) Interest payable on coupon debenture is treated as a charge against the profits of the company[cite: 13].

question_html: What is the effect on the accounting records when Method 1 is used for issuing debentures as collateral security?

options.A: Debentures Suspense Account is debited and Debentures Account is credited.
options.B: No entry is made in the books of account of the company at the time of issuing such debentures, and the fact is disclosed in Notes to Accounts[cite: 13].
options.C: Bank Loan Account is debited with debenture face value.
options.D: A contingent liability account is credited.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Under Method 1, no entry is made in the books of account, and the issue is shown by way of a note under the liability secured[cite: 13].

question_html: Can debentures be issued for consideration other than cash, such as for purchasing land or machinery?

options.A: No, debentures can only be issued against cash subscriptions.
options.B: Yes, debentures can be issued in direct exchange for assets like land, machinery, etc.[cite: 13]
options.C: Only if approved by the Reserve Bank of India.
options.D: Only at a mandatory 10% premium.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Debentures can also be issued for consideration other than for cash, such as for purchase of land, machinery, etc.[cite: 13].
topic_text: Issue of Debentures for Consideration Other than Cash
